title: Puka Nacua Skips IR Designation, Yet Faces Extended Absence, NBC Sports Reports
body:
Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua will remain sidelined for an indeterminate stretch of the season, even though the team has opted not to place him on injured reserve. The decision underscores the mounting injury crisis that has already forced the Rams to juggle a dwindling number of roster spots for players returning from IR, and it raises fresh questions about depth and strategic flexibility as the franchise fights to stay competitive in a tightly contested NFC West.

Nacua, a second‑year talent who burst onto the scene with a string of clutch catches late last season, suffered a soft‑tissue injury during a routine practice drill in early October. Team physicians determined that the damage is more severe than initially believed, but they also concluded that the recovery timeline will likely exceed the 21‑day window required for a short‑term IR designation. By keeping him on the active roster, the Rams preserve the option to reactivate him quickly should his rehab progress faster than expected, but they also sacrifice a valuable slot that could be used to promote a practice‑squad player or sign a free‑agent depth piece.

The Rams’ injury ledger this year reads like a cautionary tale for any NFL organization. Starting quarterback Matthew Stafford has missed several games with a lingering shoulder issue, left tackle Jonathan “Junior” Taylor is out with a high‑ankle sprain, and defensive stalwart Aaron Donald is nursing a calf strain that has limited his pass‑rush production. The cumulative effect has left the roster thin in several key positions, prompting head coach Sean McVay to lean heavily on younger, less experienced players. In that context, Nacua’s absence is felt not just in the passing game but also in the team’s ability to stretch defenses and create space for the running attack.

From a strategic standpoint, the Rams’ decision to keep Nacua off IR reflects a broader league‑wide trend of teams using the flexible IR rules to manage roster depth. Since the NFL relaxed the IR eligibility criteria in 2020, clubs have been more willing to move players in and out of the list, balancing the need for immediate contributors with the desire to retain future options. However, the Rams are now confronting a logistical bottleneck: each time a player is placed on IR, the team loses a coveted “return” slot that can only be used a limited number of times per season. With several players already designated for short‑term IR, the window for future moves is rapidly closing.

Analysts suggest that the Rams may be forced to explore creative solutions if the injury tide does not recede. Options include signing veteran free agents to short‑term contracts, elevating practice‑squad members who have shown promise in recent workouts, or even considering a trade for a depth receiver who can fill Nacua’s role in the interim. The front office will also have to weigh the risk of rushing Nacua back against the potential loss of a key offensive weapon in the latter half of the season. In a division where the San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks have largely stayed healthy, the Rams cannot afford to let injuries dictate their destiny.

Looking ahead, the Rams’ medical staff is expected to provide a more precise timetable for Nacua’s return within the next week. If his rehabilitation proceeds as projected, the team could see him back in practice by early November, with a potential game‑day activation before the end of the month. Until then, McVay will likely continue to rely on emerging talents like Jalen McCulloch and veteran depth such as Van Jefferson to keep the passing attack afloat. The coming weeks will test the Rams’ resilience and depth, and how they navigate this injury‑laden stretch could determine whether they remain playoff contenders or slip into a rebuilding phase.
